page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processors, this configuration provides 4 physical cores and 8 virtual CPUs via multithreading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB shared L3 cache. It includes 16 GB of system RAM, allocating 2 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support spans AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration featuring AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread compute capabilities, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,867.28 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2,514.0, both placing in the top quartile. General compute throughput remains consistent across multi-threaded tasks, logging 11,479.6 in stress-ng and 7,079.0 in Geekbench multi-core. However, memory subsystem tests show constrained throughput under uncached large-block transfers, reaching 36.85 GB/sec for read and 13.83 GB/sec for write operations.

The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring attached network persistent disks for filesystem operations. Furthermore, no hardware accelerators or GPUs are included. Because of its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory footprint and capable instruction pipeline, the c3d-highcpu-8 offers high compute density per dollar for CPU-bound tasks. It is well matched for software compilation, batch processing, CI/CD runners, and text processing pipelines, while remaining less suitable for memory-bandwidth-bound analytics or large-footprint in-memory databases.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor and 16 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic extensions including VAES and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 2 GB of RAM per vCPU and includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote persistent storage. Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-core performance, particularly in stress-ng and text processing, while multi-core workloads align with expected class averages. Due to a reduced 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and lower sustained write bandwidth on large memory blocks, resource efficiency favors processing-heavy operations over memory-intensive datasets. It is well tailored for software build pipelines, batch computation, web serving, and continuous integration environments.
